facts.text: Leverage is moderate and the only borrowed debt matures in 2028, but EBITDA swings with fertilizer prices and plant downtime and most cash is distributed, so creditor protection rests on the cash balance and a small asset-based facility. Net debt was USD 411.55 million at September 30, 2026, or 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 224.73 million against 2.37x at the end of 2025, and total debt was USD 569.74 million. Quarter-end cash of USD 158.19 million was lifted by customer prepayments, and the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million would take net leverage to 1.92x once paid on November 23, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K9; calculation K16

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Total debt to EBITDA was 1.95x in FY2023, 3.18x in FY2024, 2.70x in FY2025 and 2.54x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 1.79x, 2.67x, 2.37x and 1.83x. Debt moved by only USD 22.43 million over the period, almost all of it finance lease obligations first recorded in 2024, so the swings come from EBITDA, which fell from USD 281.1 million in FY2023 to USD 178.9 million in FY2024 before recovering. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third quarter of 2026 shows how quickly cover can fall: EBITDA was USD 19.72 million against USD 70.62 million a year earlier, with turnaround expenses of USD 26.84 million against USD 1.23 million, yet nine-month EBITDA of USD 204.56 million stayed above USD 190.68 million. The East Dubuque turnaround ended in mid-October 2026, so the lost output is behind the company, but the issuer expects the expanded capacity to be tested in the fourth quarter. The fourth quarter of 2025, derived at USD 20.17 million of EBITDA, also carried a turnaround, at Coffeyville, so two of the four quarters in the last-twelve-months figure were weak and that figure already absorbs both. facts.text: Operating cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was USD 258.39 million, USD 87.15 million above the prior year, and USD 70.58 million of that rise came from working capital, chiefly customer prepayments recorded as deferred revenue and payables on turnaround projects. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus USD 45.2 million of availability under the asset-based facility, which has nothing drawn and matures in September 2028. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Control rests with CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises through the general partner, and the board's policy is to pay out all available cash, so creditor protection depends on debt covenants that are not in the evidence rather than on independent governance. The business is two nitrogen fertilizer plants selling mostly UAN and ammonia at commodity prices under contracts of less than one year, so cash flow follows prices and plant uptime. Distributions of USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow of USD 98.84 million, and the owners are weighing strategic options that could involve the Partnership; a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could trigger a repurchase offer on the notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 47–53; calculation A1; calculation A5

The business is two nitrogen fertilizer plants selling mostly UAN and ammonia at commodity prices under contracts of less than one year, so cash flow follows prices and plant uptime. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control is concentrated and creditors have no governance voice. CVR Energy holds about 37% of the units and all of the general partner, and Icahn Enterprises owns about 71% of CVR Energy and so is treated by the issuer as holding about 40% of the units beneficially. Unitholders do not elect the general partner or its directors, the partnership agreement replaces default fiduciary duties with narrower contractual ones, and the board rests on exemptions from the exchange's independence rules, so the only checks on owner decisions that creditors can rely on are the debt documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 121

Four directors, three of them independent, were removed that month, the board is chaired by a current Icahn Enterprises employee, and at the end of 2025 the board of six held three independent directors, short of a majority, while a two-person special committee of the chair and the chief executive could approve urgent matters between board meetings at the date of the annual report. The documents give no reason for the removals. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 121–122; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Related-party arrangements are a dependency as well as a cost. CVR Energy's refinery supplied about 36% of the pet coke used in 2025, the services agreement that provides management and administration can be ended on 90 days' notice, and the Coffeyville feedstock and hydrogen agreement ends automatically if the two parties fall out of common control. Charges to the Partnership were about USD 42.32 million in FY2025, 8.89% of cost of sales and administrative expense, and the CVR Energy subsidiary line rose from USD 8.9 million to USD 14.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, so a change of control would reach supply and services as well as the notes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A4

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Distribution policy leaks cash in weak years but has not been debt funded. The board distributes available cash after reserves it sets in its sole discretion, and about 39% goes to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises. Distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025 and were met from cash, while borrowed debt stayed at the notes alone; in the first nine months of 2026 free cash flow of USD 193.88 million covered distributions of USD 110.45 million. The declared third-quarter distribution of USD 18.9 million follows a quarter in which USD 64.26 million was paid. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A7

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Event risk comes from the owners' strategic review and the change-of-control terms, not from any disclosed transaction. CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises say they are considering strategic transactions that may include options involving the Partnership, with no terms or timetable. A sale or transfer of some or all of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes, with a repurchase offer at 101%, and an event of default under the asset-based facility; the owners' general partner can also buy out public unitholders if it and its affiliates ever hold more than 80% of the units, which is far from the 40% held. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation A5

facts.text: Management is in transition. The chief executive named in the first-quarter release was succeeded by the chief financial officer by the second-quarter release, the second and third quarterly reports are signed by an interim chief financial officer, and executives are employed through CVR Energy, which sets the pay of every executive officer except the chief executive. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The operating model is a commodity price-taker with feedstock and plant concentration. Product sales are mostly UAN and ammonia under wholesale contracts of less than one year, the top two customers took 28% of FY2025 net sales, sales are heavier in the first half of each year, and each plant is a single site, so a turnaround or outage hits EBITDA in the quarter. Customers also prepay, which lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026 from USD 43.6 million at the end of 2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation A3; calculation A8

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern is conduct: the documents read report no debt-funded distribution, no amendment or exchange of the notes, no drop-down of assets to an unrestricted subsidiary and no payment to the owners beyond their pro rata share of distributions and the charges under the service agreements, borrowed debt has been the one note issue since 2021, and the board sets reserves. The chain of ownership is also stable, with the shares of the holders unchanged to the level the filings print. That view would win if the owners' review ends without a transaction and the executed debt documents show tight restricted-payment and affiliate-transaction limits. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation A6; calculation A7

facts.label: T2D.9 Risk-level driver table
facts.text: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by owner control, a variable distribution policy that paid out more than free cash flow in two of the last three years, and change-of-control exposure, because owners can change policy or transact without a creditor check, which implies lower liquidity in a downturn and event risk on a control change. Countervailing evidence is the absence of debt-funded distributions, a stable single-instrument capital structure and audited reporting; further analysis needs the executed debt documents and the terms of any transaction. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Fundamental credit quality is adequate but volatile: moderate leverage, fixed-rate notes due in 2028 and liquidity of USD 203.4 million support creditors, while commodity-priced earnings and an owner-controlled payout leave little margin for a price or uptime shock. Net debt was 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and interest cover was 6.10x, yet EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, and distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025. The primary downside path is a price or outage shock that cuts EBITDA while distributions continue; a change of control would add a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million against liquidity of USD 203.4 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B8; calculation B13

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings are the weakest dimension: revenue is exposed to commodity prices and plant uptime, and fixed plant costs turn a modest revenue move into a large EBITDA move. In FY2024 revenue fell 22.91% and EBITDA fell 36.36%, 1.59 times as fast, because direct operating expenses fell only 8.32%; EBITDA then recovered to USD 210.85 million in FY2025 and USD 224.73 million for the last twelve months. facts.text: CVR Partners makes and sells nitrogen fertilizer, mainly UAN and ammonia, from two plants: Coffeyville, Kansas, which gasifies pet coke, and East Dubuque, Illinois, which runs on natural gas. facts.text: The Partnership is a listed limited partnership controlled by CVR Energy through the general partner, with Icahn Enterprises owning about 71% of CVR Energy. facts.text: The scenario is a nitrogen price fall or a plant outage of the kind that cut FY2024 EBITDA. Leverage rises and cover falls as shown in the illustration, the facility's availability of USD 45.2 million is the next buffer, and the notes become current in mid-2027 while earnings are weak. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is moderate and the only borrowed debt matures in 2028, but EBITDA swings with fertilizer prices and plant downtime and most cash is distributed, so creditor protection rests on the cash balance and a small asset-based facility.

Net debt was USD 411.55 million at September 30, 2026, or 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 224.73 million against 2.37x at the end of 2025, and total debt was USD 569.74 million. Quarter-end cash of USD 158.19 million was lifted by customer prepayments, and the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million would take net leverage to 1.92x once paid on November 23, 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K9; calculation K16
### Key findings

Total debt to EBITDA was 1.95x in FY2023, 3.18x in FY2024, 2.70x in FY2025 and 2.54x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and net debt to EBITDA was 1.79x, 2.67x, 2.37x and 1.83x. Debt moved by only USD 22.43 million over the period, almost all of it finance lease obligations first recorded in 2024, so the swings come from EBITDA, which fell from USD 281.1 million in FY2023 to USD 178.9 million in FY2024 before recovering. The notes carry a fixed coupon, so EBITDA to cash interest of 8.25x, 5.24x, 5.74x and 6.10x moved with EBITDA alone: creditors carry commodity-cycle risk on a stable debt balance.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K16

The third quarter of 2026 shows how quickly cover can fall: EBITDA was USD 19.72 million against USD 70.62 million a year earlier, with turnaround expenses of USD 26.84 million against USD 1.23 million, yet nine-month EBITDA of USD 204.56 million stayed above USD 190.68 million. The East Dubuque turnaround ended in mid-October 2026, so the lost output is behind the company, but the issuer expects the expanded capacity to be tested in the fourth quarter. The fourth quarter of 2025, derived at USD 20.17 million of EBITDA, also carried a turnaround, at Coffeyville, so two of the four quarters in the last-twelve-months figure were weak and that figure already absorbs both.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation K17

Operating cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was USD 258.39 million, USD 87.15 million above the prior year, and USD 70.58 million of that rise came from working capital, chiefly customer prepayments recorded as deferred revenue and payables on turnaround projects. After cash capital expenditures of USD 64.51 million the free cash flow of USD 193.88 million funded distributions of USD 110.45 million and left cash USD 88.95 million higher. The working-capital inflow reverses as product ships, and the filings do not say how much of the cash balance is customer advances.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation K6; calculation K7

Deferred revenue, a non-interest-bearing float that funds operations, stood at USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 43.6 million at the end of 2025. Customers have prepaid against future deliveries, so part of the cash buffer is owed in product rather than available to creditors.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation K8

Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus USD 45.2 million of availability under the asset-based facility, which has nothing drawn and matures in September 2028. Calls on it in the next quarter are the distribution of USD 18.9 million, fourth-quarter capital spending that the full-year estimate implies at USD 29.11 million to USD 38.11 million (the release outlook is USD 26 million to USD 34 million), and the semi-annual note coupon due in December. No principal on the notes or the facility falls due within twelve months: the notes mature in June 2028 and have been callable at par since June 15, 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105; calculation K9; calculation K13

The debt total depends on perimeter. Total debt of USD 569.74 million includes finance lease obligations of USD 20.86 million, and the issuer's own long-term debt line for the notes alone is USD 548.88 million, which would read as 2.44x rather than 2.54x total debt to EBITDA. Capital expenditures also carry two bases, USD 64.51 million paid in cash and USD 65.89 million on the table basis, and every ratio here uses carrying value and the cash basis unless stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation K3; calculation K10; calculation K12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet: net leverage of 1.83x is below the 2.67x of FY2024 and the 2.37x of FY2025, interest cover of 6.10x is above FY2024 and FY2025, and liquidity of USD 203.4 million is well above USD 117.1 million at the end of 2025. That view would win if the third-quarter earnings loss proves a one-off turnaround effect and the East Dubuque expansion lifts output as planned.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation K1; calculation K2

The view would turn negative on a change of control, which the 2025 annual report says could follow a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy: the 101% repurchase offer on the notes would call for about USD 555.5 million before accrued interest, against liquidity of USD 203.4 million, and the executed indenture that would settle the terms is not in the evidence. A fourth-quarter EBITDA that fails to recover from the USD 19.72 million of the third quarter, or capital spending at the top of the implied USD 38.11 million, would also draw down the cash that supports liquidity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation K11; calculation K13
### Limitations

The executed indenture, ABL agreement and intercreditor agreement are not in the evidence, so security, guarantor scope and covenant levels are taken from filing summaries only. The three 2026 quarterly reports are unaudited, the fourth quarter of 2025 is not stated on its own, and last-twelve-months figures are derived by addition and subtraction rather than reported.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 172–175; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 7

Undrawn facility capacity at the end of 2023 is stated by the issuer to one decimal only, the borrowing base behind the facility's availability is not disclosed, and interim income tax lines are printed as dashes that this analysis does not read as zero. No adjusted EBITDA is stated apart from EBITDA, so every ratio uses the issuer's single EBITDA measure.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 7

## Gaps

- The executed indenture, ABL credit agreement and intercreditor agreement are not supplied, so security, guarantor scope, covenant levels, change-of-control terms and lien ranking rest on filing summaries; this restricts any covenant or recovery conclusion. Severity High. Action: obtain the executed documents with their amendments.

- The ABL's availability of USD 45.202 million is below its USD 50.0 million commitment with nothing drawn, and the borrowing base is not disclosed, so changes in availability cannot be explained; this restricts the liquidity view. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the latest borrowing base certificate.

- Undrawn ABL capacity at the end of 2023 is stated by the issuer only as USD 39.0 million to one decimal, so the FY2023 liquidity row is rounded at source. Severity Low. Action: none needed beyond the stated precision.

- The income tax line is printed as a dash in the four interim columns and is held as not supplied rather than zero; EBITDA is the issuer's stated figure, so no ratio is affected. Severity Low. Action: none.

- Funds from operations and distributable cash flow are neither defined nor stated in the filings, so funds from operations to debt and distributable cash flow to debt are not calculable; Available Cash for Distribution is set by the Board with reserves and is not a substitute. Severity Low. Action: none unless the issuer defines the measures.

- Several cash flow lines appear in the annual statements and not the interim ones, or the reverse (amortization of deferred financing costs, loss on asset disposals, proceeds from asset sales, other investing activities, principal payments of finance leases, other financing activities), and a few are printed as dashes; each is held as not supplied rather than zero, and the totals reconcile, so no ratio is affected. Severity Low. Action: none.

- The finance lease obligation's rate, security and maturity profile are not tabulated here and the debt note gives no principal for it; the instrument table holds those cells as not supplied. Severity Low. Action: read the leases note if lease terms are needed.

- The legal rank of the ABL and the finance lease obligation relative to the notes is not stated in the summaries read, so the debt stack holds only the notes. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the intercreditor agreement.

- The fourth quarter of 2025 is not stated on its own and is derived as the fiscal year less nine months; no figure of it is used in a ratio. Severity Low. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release if a stated figure is wanted.

- The issuer prints a single EBITDA figure under the name EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, so no separate adjusted measure, adjusted ratios or EBITDA bridge can be stated. Severity Low. Action: none unless the issuer adds adjustments.

- Fourth-quarter 2026 capital expenditures are USD 26 million to USD 34 million in the release outlook and USD 29.111 million to USD 38.111 million when the full-year estimate is reduced by nine-month spending, and the filings do not reconcile them. Severity Low. Action: ask the issuer which basis the full-year estimate uses.

- The distribution per unit in the third-quarter release row headed declared is the amount paid in the quarter under the quarterly report, while the amount declared for the quarter is USD 1.79; the two are kept apart. Severity Low. Action: none.

- Distribution payment on 2026-11-23 and anything after 2026-11-03 are not confirmed by any document, so the pro forma figure is scheduled, not realised. Severity Low. Action: obtain later current reports if any exist.

- The first-quarter and second-quarter 2026 reports and releases are read but not tabulated, so no discrete first-half 2026 column exists; nine-month and third-quarter columns are provided. Severity Low. Action: add columns if a quarterly trend is wanted.

## Request

Business and governance fact pack for Cvr Partners, Lp (CVR Partners, LP in its filings; issuer id uan-1425292), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, operating model, ownership, control, related-party arrangements, owner behaviour and history from the eight supplied filings and releases, with no specified transaction in the evidence.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Control rests with CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises through the general partner, and the board's policy is to pay out all available cash, so creditor protection depends on debt covenants that are not in the evidence rather than on independent governance.

The business is two nitrogen fertilizer plants selling mostly UAN and ammonia at commodity prices under contracts of less than one year, so cash flow follows prices and plant uptime. Distributions of USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow of USD 98.84 million, and the owners are weighing strategic options that could involve the Partnership; a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could trigger a repurchase offer on the notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 47–53; calculation A1; calculation A5
### Key findings

Control is concentrated and creditors have no governance voice. CVR Energy holds about 37% of the units and all of the general partner, and Icahn Enterprises owns about 71% of CVR Energy and so is treated by the issuer as holding about 40% of the units beneficially. Unitholders do not elect the general partner or its directors, the partnership agreement replaces default fiduciary duties with narrower contractual ones, and the board rests on exemptions from the exchange's independence rules, so the only checks on owner decisions that creditors can rely on are the debt documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 121

The board changed shape in October 2025, which tightens owner control. Four directors, three of them independent, were removed that month, the board is chaired by a current Icahn Enterprises employee, and at the end of 2025 the board of six held three independent directors, short of a majority, while a two-person special committee of the chair and the chief executive could approve urgent matters between board meetings at the date of the annual report. The documents give no reason for the removals.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 121–122; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128

Related-party arrangements are a dependency as well as a cost. CVR Energy's refinery supplied about 36% of the pet coke used in 2025, the services agreement that provides management and administration can be ended on 90 days' notice, and the Coffeyville feedstock and hydrogen agreement ends automatically if the two parties fall out of common control. Charges to the Partnership were about USD 42.32 million in FY2025, 8.89% of cost of sales and administrative expense, and the CVR Energy subsidiary line rose from USD 8.9 million to USD 14.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, so a change of control would reach supply and services as well as the notes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A4

Distribution policy leaks cash in weak years but has not been debt funded. The board distributes available cash after reserves it sets in its sole discretion, and about 39% goes to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises. Distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025 and were met from cash, while borrowed debt stayed at the notes alone; in the first nine months of 2026 free cash flow of USD 193.88 million covered distributions of USD 110.45 million. The declared third-quarter distribution of USD 18.9 million follows a quarter in which USD 64.26 million was paid.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A7

Event risk comes from the owners' strategic review and the change-of-control terms, not from any disclosed transaction. CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises say they are considering strategic transactions that may include options involving the Partnership, with no terms or timetable. A sale or transfer of some or all of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes, with a repurchase offer at 101%, and an event of default under the asset-based facility; the owners' general partner can also buy out public unitholders if it and its affiliates ever hold more than 80% of the units, which is far from the 40% held.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation A5

Management is in transition. The chief executive named in the first-quarter release was succeeded by the chief financial officer by the second-quarter release, the second and third quarterly reports are signed by an interim chief financial officer, and executives are employed through CVR Energy, which sets the pay of every executive officer except the chief executive. The partnership bears these costs through service fees and the filings do not show a cost of the transition.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_uan_exhibit991-uanq12026earnin-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_uan_exhibit991-uanq22026earnin-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 52

The operating model is a commodity price-taker with feedstock and plant concentration. Product sales are mostly UAN and ammonia under wholesale contracts of less than one year, the top two customers took 28% of FY2025 net sales, sales are heavier in the first half of each year, and each plant is a single site, so a turnaround or outage hits EBITDA in the quarter. Customers also prepay, which lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026 from USD 43.6 million at the end of 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation A3; calculation A8
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is conduct: the documents read report no debt-funded distribution, no amendment or exchange of the notes, no drop-down of assets to an unrestricted subsidiary and no payment to the owners beyond their pro rata share of distributions and the charges under the service agreements, borrowed debt has been the one note issue since 2021, and the board sets reserves. The chain of ownership is also stable, with the shares of the holders unchanged to the level the filings print. That view would win if the owners' review ends without a transaction and the executed debt documents show tight restricted-payment and affiliate-transaction limits.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation A6; calculation A7

The view would turn negative on any disclosed transaction that moves control of CVR Energy or the general partner, on a distribution that exceeds free cash flow while liquidity is falling, or on a further change to the board that removes independent directors. Each would act through the 101% repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million against liquidity of USD 203.4 million, the termination rights in the services and feedstock agreements, and the loss of the cash buffer.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation A1; calculation A5
### Limitations

- The partnership agreement, the indenture and the asset-based facility agreement are not in the evidence, so restricted-payment, affiliate-transaction and change-of-control limits cannot be read, which stops any view on whether the owners' capacity to extract cash is constrained.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 172–175; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 106

- The documents give no reason for the October 2025 board changes and no terms of the strategic review, so the view that control has tightened and the event-risk finding rest on disclosed facts only and say nothing on owner intent.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 19
- Ownership percentages after 2025 are printed to whole numbers, so small changes in the Icahn Enterprises holding cannot be seen, which limits the finding that the holdings are stable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation A6

- Related-party charges are shown in total only, with no breakdown of the Corporate service fee by service and no market comparison, so the finding that the cost is modest cannot be tested against arm's-length terms.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16

## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Cvr Partners, Lp (CVR Partners, LP in its filings; issuer id uan-1425292), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, cash-flow durability, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy and the main downside path from the eight supplied filings and releases and the three earlier modules, without a rating, security view or legal-capacity conclusion.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate but volatile: moderate leverage, fixed-rate notes due in 2028 and liquidity of USD 203.4 million support creditors, while commodity-priced earnings and an owner-controlled payout leave little margin for a price or uptime shock.

Net debt was 1.83x last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and interest cover was 6.10x, yet EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, and distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2023 and FY2025. The primary downside path is a price or outage shock that cuts EBITDA while distributions continue; a change of control would add a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million against liquidity of USD 203.4 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B8; calculation B13
### Key findings

Earnings are the weakest dimension: revenue is exposed to commodity prices and plant uptime, and fixed plant costs turn a modest revenue move into a large EBITDA move. In FY2024 revenue fell 22.91% and EBITDA fell 36.36%, 1.59 times as fast, because direct operating expenses fell only 8.32%; EBITDA then recovered to USD 210.85 million in FY2025 and USD 224.73 million for the last twelve months. Customers contract for less than one year at fixed prices, the top two took 28% of FY2025 sales, and a turnaround or outage hits a single site.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 113; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B4; calculation B13

Leverage is moderate and the debt is fixed rate, which is the strongest support. Total debt to EBITDA ranged from 1.95x in FY2023 to 3.18x in FY2024 and stood at 2.54x on the last-twelve-months basis, with net leverage of 1.83x; because the notes carry a fixed coupon, cover of EBITDA to cash interest moved only with EBITDA, from 5.24x at the low in FY2024 to 6.10x. Debt of USD 569.74 million includes finance lease obligations, and no principal falls due before June 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 104–106; calculation B1; calculation B13

Cash conversion is adequate and improving but rests on rising capital spending. Free cash flow was positive in every period, USD 219.33 million in FY2023, USD 98.84 million in FY2025 and USD 148.71 million for the last twelve months, equal to 78.03%, 46.87% and 66.17% of EBITDA. Cash capital expenditures rose from USD 50.8 million in FY2025 to USD 88.08 million over the last twelve months, and the 2026 estimate sits 66.89% to 82.7% above FY2025 spending, so conversion depends on the East Dubuque expansion and reliability projects paying back.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B13

Liquidity is adequate for the next two quarters and the refinancing window is distant but not remote. Liquidity of USD 203.4 million at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 158.2 million plus availability under an undrawn asset-based facility; after the declared distribution of USD 18.9 million and fourth-quarter capital spending, cash would stand at USD 101.18 million to USD 110.18 million before any operating cash flow in the quarter. The notes mature 575 days after the as-of date and become a current liability in mid-2027, so refinancing capacity will be tested at the point the nitrogen cycle is least predictable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 104; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation B7; calculation B13

Financial policy is the second weakness. Distributions of USD 281.36 million in FY2023 and USD 125.99 million in FY2025 exceeded free cash flow and were met from cash, about 39% went to CVR Energy and Icahn Enterprises, and the board can change the policy at any time. Customer prepayments lifted deferred revenue to USD 83.93 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 53.06% of the cash balance, so part of the cash buffer is owed in product and the working-capital inflow will reverse as deliveries are made.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation B10; calculation B11; calculation B13

Event risk is concentrated in control. The owners are considering strategic options that could involve the Partnership, with no terms stated, and a sale of the Icahn interest in CVR Energy could be a change of control under the notes with a repurchase offer of about USD 555.5 million; liquidity covers 36.61% of it. Supply and services from CVR Energy also depend on common control, so a change would reach operations as well as debt, and the executed debt documents that would settle the terms are not in the evidence.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation B8; calculation B13
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is the balance sheet and the cost position. Net leverage of 1.83x is below its FY2024 and FY2025 levels, cover of 6.10x has recovered, free cash flow covered nine-month 2026 distributions, and U.S. natural gas prices keep a cost advantage for domestic producers while Middle East disruption has lifted fertilizer prices. That view would win if the East Dubuque expansion lifts output, prices stay firm through the fourth quarter and the owners' review ends without a transaction.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation B1

The view would turn negative if EBITDA fell again by the size seen in FY2024, which on last-twelve-months EBITDA would leave USD 143.03 million and take total debt to EBITDA to 3.98x and cover to 3.89x, or on any disclosed move in control. This is an illustration of the issuer's own history, not a forecast; the Downside module sets the stress properly.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B2; calculation B9; calculation B13
### Limitations

- The executed debt documents are not in the evidence, so the view on refinancing capacity and on the cost of a change of control uses summaries of the notes and the facility, which means the credit view could move materially once covenant and call terms are read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 172–175; Source readiness (CP-0)

- No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so the assessments of business strength and of capital-market access are made against the issuer's own history only, which limits how confidently the profile can be called adequate rather than strong or weak.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
The narrative steps and registers below carry the method's remaining outputs.
### Company description

CVR Partners makes and sells nitrogen fertilizer, mainly UAN and ammonia, from two plants: Coffeyville, Kansas, which gasifies pet coke, and East Dubuque, Illinois, which runs on natural gas. Revenue is wholesale, to retailers and distributors and to agricultural and industrial buyers, under contracts that generally fix price for less than one year, so revenue visibility is short and follows market prices within each season.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 12–16

Cash generation follows the planting season, with higher sales in the first half, and is interrupted every few years by a planned turnaround at each plant. The business model therefore supports cash-flow visibility for a quarter or two, not for the length of the debt, and refinancing confidence depends on where the nitrogen price cycle stands when the notes become current.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 79
### Ownership and group structure

The Partnership is a listed limited partnership controlled by CVR Energy through the general partner, with Icahn Enterprises owning about 71% of CVR Energy. Public unitholders hold about 60% of the units but cannot elect the general partner or its directors, and the board was reshaped in October 2025. The financial-policy implication is that distributions, transactions and debt decisions are owner-led, and creditors are protected by the debt documents rather than by governance.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

UAN is the largest product and is priced at the gate per ton, so revenue is a function of price, volume and mix, with no pass-through of feedstock cost. In the third quarter of 2026 lower UAN prices and ammonia volumes cut net sales by USD 17.4 million against the prior-year quarter, while for the nine months higher UAN and ammonia prices added USD 64.7 million; the revenue base is therefore cyclical and not contractually recurring, and the top two customers are 28% of sales.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins cannot be defended well under volume or price pressure because the plants carry high fixed operating costs: direct operating expenses excluding turnaround were 40.69% of FY2024 net sales against 34.21% in FY2023 after revenue fell. EBITDA margin was 41.25%, 34.06% and 34.79% in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Feedstock is a small part of cost, so margin depends mainly on price and utilization rather than input cost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 113; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B13
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Maintenance and growth capital spending are rising and turnaround costs are expensed in the quarter incurred, so conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow was 78.03% in FY2023 and 46.87% in FY2025. Management can defer growth projects and the board can cut distributions, which are the levers that protect liquidity; the issuer says it may adjust the timing or scope of growth capital projects.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B13
### Market forces, credit-translated

Rivalry is high: domestic competitors, led by a much larger nitrogen producer, and subsidised imports compete on delivered price. Buyers are sophisticated and price focused, which caps pass-through; suppliers matter because CVR Energy's refinery supplies part of the pet coke; entry and substitution threats are limited for nitrogen itself. The credit consequence is a price-taker earnings profile with no pricing power to defend cash flow in a downturn.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_uan.htm.jsonl, page 16

Regulatory and geopolitical factors do alter credit risk here: Middle East supply disruption and import tariffs have supported U.S. prices, and litigation over an October 2025 ammonia release and a Kansas environmental class action carry unquantified liability. These items change liquidity and earnings risk and so are treated as material.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are fixed-rate debt with no maturity before June 2028, moderate leverage, positive free cash flow in every period, an undrawn facility and domestic feedstock. Weaknesses are volatile EBITDA, high fixed costs, owner-controlled payouts and a short contract tenor. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the East Dubuque expansion and firm prices; threats are a price or outage shock, a change of control and the unquantified lawsuits.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 19
### Financial profile and credit quality

Assessed on the nine dimensions: scale and market position Average; competitive advantage Average; business diversification Weak, with two plants, one segment and two products; cost and capex flexibility Average, because growth projects can be deferred while direct costs are largely fixed; margin stability Weak; free cash flow stability Average; ability to refinance Average, untested and dependent on the price cycle; liquidity position Average; financial policy and governance Weak. The main supports are leverage and liquidity, the main constraints are earnings volatility and owner control, the trend in leverage is improving from FY2024, and the missing datapoints are the debt documents, ratings and peer figures.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are firm prices from supply disruption, the expansion adding about 5% of ammonia capacity and the end of the turnaround; the headwinds are a normalisation of prices, higher capital spending and the lawsuits. Over three to five years the notes mature in 2028, the Coffeyville dual-feedstock project is planned for construction in 2028 and the owners' strategic review is unresolved. Management expects fourth-quarter ammonia utilization of 88% to 93% and says nitrogen supplies remain tight, which is management language and not evidence of price direction.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_uan_d162480dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_uan_d162480dex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario is a nitrogen price fall or a plant outage of the kind that cut FY2024 EBITDA. The first operational break is lower realized gate prices or lost tons at a single site; because direct operating costs are largely fixed, EBITDA falls faster than revenue; free cash flow then drops below the distribution the board has declared, and cash covers the gap, as it did in FY2023 and FY2025. Leverage rises and cover falls as shown in the illustration, the facility's availability of USD 45.2 million is the next buffer, and the notes become current in mid-2027 while earnings are weak. The board can cut distributions and defer growth projects, which should avoid liquidity distress at current cash, but a change of control in the same window would add the repurchase offer.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B2; calculation B9; calculation B11
### Overall credit view

Overall, CVR Partners presents an adequate business profile supported by fixed-rate debt with no maturity before 2028, moderate leverage and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by commodity-priced and operationally concentrated earnings, an owner-controlled payout and unseen debt terms. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in the near term and weak through a full cycle. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the nitrogen price level and the owners' plans in 2027. The primary downside path is a price or outage shock with distributions continuing and a change of control in the same window. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, ratings and market prices.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
Fundamental credit assessment completed with limitations. Top risk: an earnings shock while distributions continue.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths, ranked. First, fixed-rate notes of USD 550.0 million with no maturity before June 2028 and an undrawn facility: interest cost is fixed, so cover of 6.10x moves only with EBITDA, and no refinancing is needed for 575 days. Second, moderate leverage of 1.83x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA, which leaves room to absorb a moderate decline. Third, positive free cash flow in every period, USD 148.71 million over the last twelve months, which funds capital spending and most distributions. Fourth, liquidity of USD 203.4 million, which comfortably exceeds the known calls of the fourth quarter.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uan.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B13

Weaknesses, ranked. First, volatile EBITDA on high fixed costs: EBITDA fell 36.36% in FY2024 on a revenue fall of 22.91%, which is the path to a liquidity or refinancing problem. Second, owner control with a variable distribution policy that exceeded free cash flow in two of three fiscal years, so creditors rely on cash rather than retained earnings. Third, change-of-control exposure of about USD 555.5 million with owners reviewing options. Fourth, rising capital spending and a working-capital inflow from prepayments that will reverse. Fifth, unseen debt documents and no ratings or market prices.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B2; calculation B8; calculation B11; calculation B13

- No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so market access and relative strength cannot be assessed outside the issuer's own history. Severity Medium. Action: supply ratings, quotes and peers.

- The borrowing base behind the facility's availability is not disclosed, so the facility cannot be assumed to be fully available in a downturn. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the latest borrowing base certificate.

- The fixed and variable split of plant costs is not disclosed; the fixed-cost reading comes from the response of direct operating expenses to the FY2024 revenue fall. Severity Low. Action: ask the issuer for the cost split.

- Quantitative monitoring thresholds are not available in the provided materials, so the triggers carry reference points from the issuer's own history. Severity Low. Action: set thresholds with the covenant documents.
- The downside illustration uses a single historical decline and holds debt and interest unchanged. Severity Low. Action: use the Downside module for a full stress.
